question: the production card runs 12 names and the executable ticket runs 5. Put both live widths on the same ruler and say whether the gap between them is inside the disagreement between the two published engines.

units.gap_pp: pp of CAGR, card width minus ticket width, paired by phase
units.rung_disagreement_pp: |atlas 5->12 rung - capacity 5->12 rung| (a difference minus a difference)
units.level_gap_pp: |atlas cell - capacity cell| at the same width: reported, never used as the gate, because a level is not a rung

rule.frozen: written before the first read of the two live faces: the comparator is the difference-of-differences (this rung on the atlas engine vs the same rung on the capacity engine), never a level gap, because a level gap and a difference are different units

aggregation.note: the ladder's rung is a difference of two medians; the same rung taken across paired phases is a different number, and the gap between the two is the aggregation, not the book

resolution.note: minimum paired difference this cycle could detect at 80% power (two-sided 5%). A gap under it is not evidence of no difference; it is evidence that this pairing cannot tell the two widths apart

coincidences.note: the beta-rule width effect (-1.530pp) equals the capacity engine's 5->12 rung (-1.530pp) to the basis point. They are different quantities on different windows -- one is a live 2x2 cell difference, the other a second engine's rung. Recording the collision so nobody reads it as confirmation

as_issued.window: ticket inception 2024-01-02, 682 bars (not the atlas window)

verdict_reasons: 20 paired phases of one R20 cycle (need >= 20)
paired gap +0.090pp (median of 20 phase differences; range -2.050..+2.890, sd 1.255)
the same rung costs +0.515pp on the atlas engine and -1.530pp on the capacity engine, a disagreement of 2.045pp with the sign flipping = True
difference of medians +0.515pp vs median of differences +0.090pp: the ladder's rung is 83% aggregation
gap is 4.4% of the engine disagreement and 1.3% of the atlas ruler 6.68pp

this pairing's own resolution is 0.786pp at 80% power (20 phases, sd 1.255), so a gap of +0.090pp is 11% of what it could have detected -- below its own ruler, so 'no difference' is not the finding either

the two live widths are not separated by their own phases AND the engine disagreement on the same rung is wider than the gap: no part of the difference between card and ticket is quotable as a width effect

as issued the two faces print 12.51pp vs 11.33pp (+1.18pp diagonal), but the 2x2 moves two knobs at once: width effect -1.53pp under the beta rule and +0.32pp under the vol rule, with an interaction of +1.85pp (bigger than both width effects = True)

COINCIDENCE, not agreement: the beta-rule width effect (-1.530pp) equals the capacity engine's 5->12 rung (-1.530pp) to the basis point. They are different quantities on different windows -- one is a live 2x2 cell difference, the other a second engine's rung. Recording the collision so nobody reads it as confirmation
